# Tobit Chapter 11 — The EMET Bible (Literal)
**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, Tobit 11 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/TOB_011_page_001.jpg

---

**11:1** And as they went near to Kaserin, which is before Nineveh,

**11:2** Raphael said, "You know how your father was left."

**11:3** "Let us run ahead before your wife and prepare the house while she is still on-the-way."

**11:4** And they both went together, and Raphael said to-him, "Take in your-hand the gall." And the dog followed after them.

**11:5** Now Anna was sitting and looking down the-road for her son.

**11:6** And she saw him coming and said to his-father, "Look — your son is coming and the man who was traveling with him!"

**11:7** And Raphael said to Tobias before he drew-near to his-father, "I know that his eyes will be-opened.

**11:8** Apply the gall from the fish on his eyes; the medicine will work and will dissolve the white-films [that are] on his eyes, and your father will see the light."

**11:9** And Anna ran and fell on the-neck-of her-son and said to-him, "I have-seen you, child; from now on I can die!" And she wept.

**11:10** And Tobit arose and stumbled, going out through the-door-of the-courtyard; and Tobias went toward-him

**11:11** — carrying the gall in his-hand — and he blew-on-it and held-it and applied-it to his-father's eyes, saying, "Take-heart, father."

**11:12** And he put-on [the medicine] and it stung. And he rubbed-out with both-his-hands the-corners-of his-eyes, and the white-films peeled-off from the-corners-of his-eyes.

**11:13** And Tobit saw his-son and fell on his-neck and wept and said to-him, "I have-seen you, child — the light-of my eyes." And he blessed God

**11:14** and said, "Blessed [are] you, O God, and blessed [is] your name forever and ever, and blessed [are] all your holy angels.

**11:15** Because you afflicted me, yet you have had mercy on me; and now I see Tobias my-son!" And his-son went in rejoicing, and he told his-father the great-things that had-happened to-him in Media.

**11:16** And Tobit went out to-meet his-daughter-in-law at-the-gate-of Nineveh rejoicing and blessing God. And those who saw him going were-astonished, because he was walking. And Tobit gave-praise before them, because God had shown-mercy on him.

**11:17** And when Tobit drew-near to Sarah his-daughter-in-law, he blessed her and said, "Welcome, daughter — blessed is your God who brought you to us, daughter. And blessed [is] your father and blessed [is] my son Tobias, and blessed [are] you, daughter. Come in with-joy to your house, with blessing and with-joy. Come-in, daughter."

**11:18** And there was-joy on-that-day among all the Jews who were in Nineveh.

**11:19** And Ahikar and Nadab, his-kinsmen, came to rejoice-with Tobit. And the-wedding-feast-of Tobias was celebrated with-joy seven days, and many gifts were-given to-him.

---
## EMET's Textual Notes

Chapter 11 is the culmination of the healing arc begun in chapter 2 when Tobit was blinded. Key textual observations:

- **11:1**: "Kaserin" — a place name before Nineveh; rendered as a proper noun without emendation.
- **11:4**: "The dog followed" — the dog, mentioned in 6:2 when they departed, returns here. It is a small but theologically significant detail in Tobit, suggesting the faithfulness of the journey.
- **11:8**: "White-films" (leukōmata) — the Greek medical term for the opaque film covering blind eyes. EMET preserves "white-films" as more precise than "cataracts" (which is a modern medical category).
- **11:9**: "Fell on the neck" (epepesen epi ton trachēlon) — an embracing formula found also at Gen 45:14 (Joseph); EMET renders it literally to preserve the biblical resonance.
- **11:11**: "He blew on it" — the Greek enephusēsen suggests either blowing gently or applying with breath; the gesture may have ritual/healing connotations.
- **11:12**: "Rubbed out" (aneptuxen) — peeled or stripped away; EMET renders literally to preserve the physicality of the healing.
- **11:14-15**: Tobit's blessing is a short doxology. EMET preserves its structure as parallel declarations.
- **11:19**: Ahikar is Tobit's nephew, mentioned in 1:21-22 as a courtier of Esarhaddon; his appearance at the end provides narrative closure.

*— EMET*
